The provided text offers a powerful reflection on George Orwell's '1984', highlighting how the novel's depiction of a surveillance state and totalitarianism remains disturbingly relevant today. I find the author's observation particularly compelling because it underscores the enduring nature of Orwell's warnings, suggesting that the dystopian elements he foresight are not just historical fiction but a mirror to current global trends. This resonance between the text and contemporary reality is what makes the work so chilling and significant.

The river that runs through London is the Thames.
